Funding sequence

FS-01 / The order

Each bank reads the applications sent before it, so the order sets how much you get.

Your own file already decides what has to happen before the first one goes out.

  • Fundhub prints these five order rules on every lender list it builds for a client.
  • Flip the order, and the very same five come back declined, each one leaving an inquiry for the next bank to read.
  • Every bank you apply to reads the applications that went out before it. So the ORDER you send them in decides how much funding you walk away with.
  • Your own file already decides what has to happen before the first one goes out. This is section three of the lender list Fundhub builds for each client.
  • It lays out five rules. The card balance gets fixed first, the lowest score floor goes first, and only ONE application goes out at a time.
  • Then you work up the list, and personal goes before business. Flip that order around, and the very same five come back DECLINED.
  • Each of those denials still drops a hard inquiry on your report, and whichever bank comes next has all of them in front of it when it makes its call.
  • The wrong order turns the money for your next hire, your bigger job or your ads into a pile of denial letters.

FS-02 / Personal first

Every business amount starts from your personal file, so your personal file goes first.

  • Our system figures every business amount from the card funding your personal file supports.
  • A company two years or older counts at double that amount, and one under a year counts at half.
  • Underneath that order sits one rule inside our system. Every business amount starts from the card funding your PERSONAL file supports.
  • A stronger personal file raises the amount for every business you add, so nothing else gets worked until your personal file is READY.
  • Then each business gets counted by its age. A company two years or older counts at DOUBLE your personal card funding, and one under a year counts at half.
  • After that, every company is judged by itself. If you don't have a company yet, your path runs from personal funding straight to the banks.
  • Every company you add later gets figured from that same personal file. So the work you put into it now shows up again in each one of them.

FS-03 / One at a time

Once inquiries pile up on one report, banks start saying no, so we send one at a time.

  • Each application waits for the last bank's answer before it goes out, so your pulls land one at a time.
  • That's rule three on your lender list, and it protects every application that comes after it.
  • What happens when five applications go out the same afternoon? Each one drops a HARD inquiry on your report, and every bank can see all of them.
  • Each inquiry shows who pulled your file and on what date. So the next bank knows how many went out, and how recently they went.
  • When a bank sees that many fresh pulls at once, it starts declining. Rule three on your lender list is there to stop that from happening to you.
  • So one application goes out, and we WAIT for that bank's answer before the next one goes anywhere. The bank's decision sets the pace.
  • For you, every bank in the round reads your file with as few new pulls on it as possible, and that protects every application behind it.

FS-04 / Which banks

National banks go first, then the local banks where you live and where your business is.

  • Living in one state and running the business in another gets you both sets of local banks, with each bank listed once.
  • Any bank that pulls a bureau with a fresh inquiry on it gets held back, so your pulls stay spread across all three.
  • So which banks make your list? Our system builds it from your file in three bands, and it reads top to bottom in that exact ORDER.
  • National banks come first. Next come the local banks in your home state, and then the local banks in the state where your business is set up.
  • Live in one state and run the business from another? You get BOTH sets of local banks, and a bank that covers both states only shows up once.
  • When a bureau already shows a fresh inquiry, any bank that pulls that bureau gets held back. That keeps your pulls SPREAD across all three bureaus.
  • The banks and the order are our job, and the yes or no belongs to the bank. That's why every bank on your list is one your file makes sense for.

FS-05 / What it builds

Each funding sequence sets up the next one, so your growth keeps running on funding.

  • Fresh inquiries get disputed before each new round leaves, and a full funding sequence takes about six rounds.
  • Each new sequence pays for the next stage of growth, a new employee, a larger contract, more ads, with your savings left alone.
  • Round one goes out with the pulls spread across all three bureaus. Before the next round leaves, every NEW inquiry from round one gets disputed.
  • That's the sweep. The second round starts from a report where the first round's inquiries are already disputed, and a sequence keeps that up for about six rounds.
  • Once a sequence wraps up, our system marks the day your file can start the next one. The Fundhub team gets that day too, so nobody has to remember it.
  • So the employee you've been waiting to hire, the larger contract and the ads you want running get paid with funding, and your savings stay out of it.
  • I run my own funding the same way. Off one personal file, I've had $100,000 lines approved for FOUR separate companies, and each company brought in its own funding.

FS-06 / The guarantee

Applications go out within 72 business hours.

  • That's our guarantee, and it's in your contract. That typically means approvals come very shortly after.
  • Both clocks start the day you sign, and the clause says your delay never pauses either one.
  • Everything you just saw starts on a CLOCK the day you sign. That clock is printed in the agreement you read before you pay.
  • Applications go out within 72 business hours. That's our guarantee, and it's in your contract. That typically means approvals come very shortly after.
  • Read the clause with me. Inside 24 business hours of your signature, an advisor has your file open, and your first authorized applications go out inside 72.
  • The last sentence is there for YOU. If you're slow sending us something, both clocks keep running, and the pressure to deliver stays on our side.
  • Ten years and hundreds of files taught me how to run this, and the rule I hold my team to is simple: we fulfill, and we keep our word.

FS-07 / Your call

On your strategy call, you see what your file needs before the first application.

  • The soft pull happens live on the call, and your score stays right where it is.
  • You see how much you qualify for based on where you're at right now, the fix that comes first, and the order after it.
  • Remember, your file already decides what has to happen before the first application. On your strategy call, you SEE exactly what that is for your file.
  • We run the soft pull right there on the call. It doesn't touch your score, and no bank sees it, because nothing has been applied for yet.
  • Then your advisor shares the screen and walks your file with you. You see how much you qualify for based on where you're at right now, and what's holding back the rest.
  • You see which fix comes first, and the order your personal file and any business go in. Approval is always the bank's decision, and the plan is built around that.
  • From there you pick the path that fits: fund now, fix first, or both. You leave with the ORDER for your file already mapped out.
  • A computer works best for this, since you'll be reading your own report on a shared screen, line by line, with your advisor right there.
